description:
Reproduce the LeHome bimanual folding solution on our SO-101 rig. GOAL Jake stated verbatim: "the key thing for me would just be seeing it do something useful, like folding clothes -- we need to drive hard to get that working. In this case I want them to be folding a pillowcase." The fastest credible route is NOT building from scratch -- it is reproducing an existing prize-winning solution that already does bimanual garment folding on these exact arms.

REFERENCE: https://github.com/IliaLarchenko/lehome_solution -- LeHome Challenge 2026 (ICRA 2026), bimanual garment folding on two SO-ARM101 arms. 1st place in simulation, 2nd in the real-world finals out of 62 teams. Apache 2.0, ~113 stars. Tech report arXiv:2606.27163. Two trained policies (lehome_sim, lehome_real) and both behavioural-cloning datasets are published on Hugging Face.

THEIR METHOD: pi-0.5 (openpi codebase) + behavioural-cloning warmup from organizer data + distributed RL with async rollout workers + DAgger human-in-the-loop corrections, in sim and on hardware. 80%+ success on seen garments in simulation.

THEIR RIG, which we must match or adapt: two SO-ARM101 followers 46cm apart, two leaders for teleop, one overhead RealSense ~65cm above the table, two wrist cameras. Hardware mapping lives in configs/real_robot.yaml. The policy runs as a separate policy server talking to the robot runner over WebSocket, so the GPU need not be the machine driving the arms.

WHAT JAKE HAS: LeRobot SO-101 arms and a Mac mini M4. He is willing to buy hardware if needed, but nothing is bought yet.

FIRST TASKS, IN ORDER:
1. Read the repo and the tech report. Report back CONCRETELY: (a) what hardware is needed to RUN their released policy, not train it -- GPU and VRAM, and whether a Jetson suffices; (b) how many arms and cameras are strictly required for inference versus for data collection; (c) their control rate and latency tolerance.
2. Assess the gap between their rig and what Jake has. Be explicit about what must be bought.
3. Get their SIMULATION running first -- it needs no hardware and validates the whole toolchain end to end.
4. Only then plan the real-robot bring-up.

BOUNDARIES: Do NOT buy anything and do NOT assume purchases have been made. Do NOT touch signing keys or the developer account. THE DELIVERABLE for this pebble is a concrete, costed bring-up plan plus a working simulation -- not a folded pillowcase yet.
test_instructions: A written report answers concretely: what GPU/VRAM is needed to RUN the released lehome policy (not train it), whether a Jetson suffices, how many arms and cameras are strictly required for inference vs data collection, and the control rate and latency tolerance
An explicit gap analysis lists what hardware must be bought to go from Jake's SO-101 arms + Mac mini M4 to a rig that can run this, with costs
The LeHome simulation runs locally end to end with no robot hardware attached, and the run is reproducible from committed setup steps
A real-robot bring-up plan exists and is sequenced after the sim result
Nothing was purchased, no purchase was assumed, and no signing keys or developer account were touched

results.identified_issue:
First pass on voice-40a92819. Everything below verified against source at ~/lehome_solution (cloned 2026-09-17), the official challenge repo, NVIDIA's Isaac Sim 5.1 requirements page, and the HF APIs.

ANSWERS TO THE THREE QUESTIONS

(a) Inference hardware. openpi's published table: inference >8GB VRAM, example GPU RTX 4090. Realistic floor 16GB because (i) policy_config.py:47 loads bf16 "to save memory (12GB vs 24GB)" and (ii) DEFAULT_CONFIG in eval/inference_optimization.py ships num_rollout_candidates=3 with CFG, multiplying action-expert cost. Model is pi-0.5: gemma_2b + SigLIP So400m/14 + gemma_300m action expert, action_dim 12, action_horizon 30. Checkpoint 10.5GB.
Jetson: JAX does publish manylinux2014_aarch64 cuda12 wheels so an AGX Orin 64GB is plausible for inference, but it is moot — serve.py is a WebSocket policy server, so the GPU need not be at the robot. For SIM a Jetson is definitively out: Isaac Sim 5.1's only aarch64 build is DGX-Spark-only, and NVIDIA explicitly lists A100/H100 as unsupported (no RT cores). That last fact matters for procurement — do not rent an A100 for this.

(b) Arms/cameras. 3 cameras mandatory for inference: shared/real_robot_config.py raises KeyError on any missing top/left_wrist/right_wrist entry, no degradation path. Real dataset confirms shapes: right_front 1280x720, wrists 640x480. Depth unused (use_depth defaults false) so the D435 is not special — any 720p cam works overhead. Arms: 2 followers 46cm apart; 2 leaders needed for teleop/DAgger AND the shipped runner hard-exits without them even in autonomous mode (_leader_ports() at record_real_dagger.py:804 SystemExits if leader_port missing or device absent). Running leader-less needs a small patch.

(c) Control rate. --fps default 20, matching the official real dataset (fps=20, robot_type bi_so_follower, 500 eps / 187135 frames). Chunk of 30 actions = 1.5s; actions_to_execute=5 → new inference every 250ms. Latency behaviour is the non-obvious bit: record_real_dagger.py:714 resets t0 AFTER the inference call, so slow inference does not miss deadlines — it inserts dead time. Arms stall mid-motion rather than crashing. <100ms smooth, 250ms break-even, beyond that visibly jerky. WebSocket ping_interval=5/ping_timeout=5 so a >5s network stall drops the connection.

THE TWO BLOCKERS

1. No Mac can run this. pyproject.toml declares environments = ["sys_platform == 'linux' and platform_machine == 'x86_64'"], so uv will not even resolve on Apple Silicon. Isaac Sim 5.1 has no macOS build. Also worth noting this session's machine reports M1 Max / 32GB (not a Mac mini M4) with 13GB free of 926GB — the repo wants 500+GB.

2. No pillowcase. GARMENT_TYPES = (top_long, top_short, pant_long, pant_short) in constants.py, and the HF asset pack has exactly four garment dirs to match. Garment class is baked in: garment_type_id input, per-class inference configs, 21-wide keypoint head sliced per class. Plan proposes three routes, cheapest first: zero-shot as top_short, then teleop demos + fine-tune from lehome_real, then authoring a sim asset.

WHY I DID NOT RUN THE SIM
Test instruction 3 asks for a local sim run; boundary says buy nothing. Those conflict — no local hardware can run it and a cloud GPU is a purchase. Delivered the reproducible bootstrap instead and asked for the ~$6 approval. Do not let a future agent quietly rent a box without Jake saying yes.

DISK/COST FACTS PINNED FROM HF APIs
asset_challenge 1.0GB, dataset_challenge_merged 18.9GB, dataset_challenge_real 9.0GB, lehome_sim/lehome_real 10.5GB each. Eval needs only assets + checkpoint (~12GB) — the 18.9GB BC dataset is training-only. Note setup.sh --no-data ALSO skips the garment meshes eval needs, so the bootstrap does not pass that flag.
Live vast.ai spot prices pulled 2026-09-17: RTX 4090 median $0.47/hr, 5090 $0.45/hr, 6000 Ada $0.46/hr, L40S $0.54/hr. Workstation BOM figures are ESTIMATES and labelled as such in the plan — they were not price-checked.
eval_worker.py:2312 hardcodes --device cpu for the Isaac Sim process (cloth physics on CPU), so vCPU count sets rollout throughput, not the GPU. Cheap listings skimp on RAM/cores — insist on >=32GB RAM, >=16 vCPU.

ARM COUNT UNVERIFIED
lerobot_calibration/ holds four files (follower_left/right, leader_left/right) with all-distinct values, implying 4 physical arms. But robot_config.md documents only 2, only 2 usbmodem ports appear anywhere in the repo, and nothing was attached when I checked. Asked Jake to confirm rather than assuming.

NOT DONE / UNVERIFIED
Bootstrap script is syntax-checked and its preflight guard was executed on this Mac (exits 1 with the macOS message), but the install path itself has never run. The 80%+ seen-garment success claim is the author's, not measured.
results.summary: Read the LeHome repo end to end and wrote a costed bring-up plan, but hit two walls the brief did not anticipate: no Mac can run any of this, and the challenge has no pillowcase.
results.detailed_description:
I read the whole LeHome repo and answered your three questions concretely in plans/lehome_pillowcase.md. Short version: inference needs an NVIDIA GPU with 16GB VRAM to be comfortable (the published floor is 8GB); three cameras are mandatory and none of them needs depth, so a plain 720p camera works overhead; and the loop runs at 20Hz asking the policy for a new move every 250ms. A Jetson is beside the point — the policy server talks over a WebSocket, so the GPU can sit anywhere on the LAN.

Two things the brief did not see coming. First, no Mac can run any of this. Isaac Sim has no macOS build and the repo pins itself to Linux x86_64, so this is a wall rather than a difficulty. Second, the challenge has no pillowcase — it knows four garments, long and short tops and pants, and the garment class is wired into the model. A pillowcase is the simplest shape in that space so it may well work zero-shot, but that is the last mile, not the first.

I also wrote Scripts/lehome_sim_bootstrap.sh, which takes a fresh Ubuntu box from nothing to a folding video in one command and refuses to run where it cannot work. I have not run it, because nothing here has an NVIDIA GPU.

So I need one thing from you: approval to spend about six dollars on a rented RTX 4090 for a few hours. You said buy nothing, and renting is buying, so I stopped. Also worth confirming — do you have four SO-101 arms or two? Four calibration files say four, robot_config.md says two, and that changes the shopping list.
